irrational-square-root.label: Square diagonal d
irrational-square-root.description: The ratio of a square’s diagonal to its side is the positive square root of two. It is irrational: no ratio of integers equals it. Consecutive finite continued-fraction convergents give useful rational approximations without turning that irrational length into a rational number.

golden-ratio.label: Golden rectangle long side L
golden-ratio.description: A golden rectangle has a long-to-short ratio φ greater than one such that removing a square leaves a rotated rectangle with the same ratio. The equality φ=1/(φ−1) gives φ²=φ+1 and φ=(1+√5)/2. Ratios of consecutive Fibonacci numbers supply finite rational comparisons.

circle-measurement.label: Disk area A
circle-measurement.description: A circle is the planar boundary at a fixed radius from its center; the disk includes its interior. The circle constant π is circumference divided by diameter. A radius r gives diameter d=2r, circumference C=2πr and disk area A=πr².

floor-ceiling.label: Containers needed N
floor-ceiling.description: Floor chooses the greatest integer no larger than a real number; ceiling chooses the least integer no smaller. Dividing liquid volume v by container capacity c gives a dimensionless quotient x. Its floor counts completely full containers, and its ceiling is the least whole count with enough capacity for the entire batch.
